summary: Hermann Ernst Grassmann studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1876 to 1880. He was a professor of mathematics at the University of Giessen from circa 1902 to 1922.

Specializing in Indology and history/archaeology, Goetz studied at the University of Munich and under mentor Jean Philippe Vogel. He held posts at Leiden University, Baroda Museum, the National Gallery of Modern Art, and Heidelberg University.
Working in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies, Güntert held academic posts at the University of Rostock (circa 1918–1921) and Heidelberg University (circa 1921–1945).

Active in Indology, linguistics, and other fields, Grassmann studied in Berlin under Friedrich Schleiermacher. He held teaching posts at the Gewerbeschule Berlin, Friedrich-Wilhelms-Gymnasium, Friedrich-Wilhelms-Schule Stettin, and Marienstiftsgymnasium, where he was a professor from 1852 to 1877.

Specializing in linguistics and Indology, Hirt studied at the University of Freiburg and Leipzig University. He taught at Leipzig University from 1891 to 1912 and was a professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Giessen from 1912 to 1936.

Specializing in history, archaeology, and linguistics, Hunger studied at the universities of Vienna, Heidelberg, and Münster. He held posts at the German Archaeological Institute, the University of Chicago, and the University of Vienna (circa 1978–2007).

Specializing in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, Jacobi studied under Albrecht Weber in Berlin and Johann Gildemeister in Bonn. He held professorships at the University of Münster, Kiel University, and the University of Bonn (1889–1922).

Kulke, an Indologist and historian, studied at Freiburg under Hermann Goetz, Madras, and Heidelberg. He held posts at Heidelberg University (1967–1988) and served as Chair of Asian History at Kiel University (1988–2003).

Active in Indology and Buddhist studies, Oldenberg studied at Göttingen and Berlin. He held professorial posts at Humboldt University of Berlin, Kiel University (where he was also Rektor), and the University of Göttingen.

Specializing in linguistics and Indology, Osthoff studied under Hermann Usener at Bonn and Georg Curtius at Leipzig. He held posts at Friedrichsgymnasium Kassel, Leipzig University, and served as Ordinarius at Heidelberg University from 1877.

A scholar in linguistics and other fields, Sauppe studied at Leipzig University under Gottfried Hermann. He served as chief librarian and professor in Zurich, director at Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium, and professor at the University of Göttingen from 1855.

Working in religious studies, linguistics, and philosophy, Usener studied at Heidelberg, Munich, Göttingen, and Bonn. He held academic posts at the University of Bern, University of Greifswald, and University of Bonn (circa 1866–1905).

A linguist who studied under August Boeckh, August Friedrich Pott, and Franz Bopp, Ebel taught at Gymnasium Schneidemühl and succeeded Bopp as chair of comparative philology at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1872.

Working in history, archaeology, and other fields, Schlagintweit studied at the University of Munich from circa 1845 to 1848 and held a teaching post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1851 to 1854.

A linguist and philosopher, Steinthal studied under August Boeckh at Humboldt University of Berlin. He later held posts at Frederick William University Berlin, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums.
Kimura, a scholar of Buddhist studies, completed doctoral studies at Taisho University circa 1978–1983 and was attested as a researcher there in 1995.

Active in Indology and Buddhist studies, Nakatani studied under Gadjin M. Nagao at Kyoto University and completed a PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He was attested as a professor at Kobe Gakuin University in 2003.
Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Kiyoshima studied at the University of Delhi and was attested as a lecturer at Kindai University in 1989.

Working in philosophy and other fields, Yukawa studied at Kyoto and Osaka universities. He held academic appointments at Osaka University, the University of Tokyo, Columbia University, and Kyoto University (circa 1939–1970).

A linguist, Tanaka studied under Raphael von Koeber at the University of Tokyo, as well as at Oxford and Kyoto. He held teaching posts at Tokyo, Kyoto University (1920–1946), and Kyoto Women's University (circa 1950–1974).
